#741. Southampton sink Middlesbrough in ill-tempered first meeting since 'Spygate'

Southampton vs Middlesbrough. EFL Championship.

St. Mary's StadiumAttendance: Attendance30,362.

Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Southampton and Middlesbrough at St Mary's on Friday night; goals from Ryan Manning and Finn Azaz earn Saints victory in first meeting since last season's 'Spygate'

Football Journalist @DanLong__

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Southampton's unbeaten start to the season at St Mary's continued as they beat leaders Middlesbrough 2-0.

Six-and-a-half months on from 'Spygate' - which dominated the headlines during last season's play-offs - Saints emerged victorious, as they did in the semi-final second leg, in an ill-tempered affair that saw 10 yellow cards brandished to players and two to coaching staff.

Had it not been for the four-point penalty imposed on them as a result, Friday night's win would have sent them to the top of the Sky Bet Championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

But goals from Ryan Manning and Finn Azaz - who goaded his former club's fans as he celebrated - put them within touching distance of the summit.

Boro's third defeat of the season opens the door to Stoke and Wolves to leapfrog them into top spot if they win on Saturday.

In the build-up, Tonda Eckert and Kim Hellberg insisted they had buried the hatchet - but neither fanbase had forgotten it. Both sets of players were booed when they came out to warm up, while chants referencing the saga echoed around St Mary's. The atmosphere was electric.

Meaningful chances came at a premium in the first half, but they were high quality when they did come.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

The home fans fell silent for a split-second when Will Lankshear ghosted away from his man and moved one-on-one with Saints goalkeeper Daniel Peretz, who denied the Championship's top scorer.

And at the other end, Radek Vitek had to be at his best, first to tip Azaz's fierce strike onto the crossbar, then to push a Cyle Larin header over.

The first goal came just before the hour. Kuryu Matsuki's cross flew over everyone in the box, but James Bree was there to collect and fizz in a low ball that Manning ran onto and side-footed high into the net.

Twenty minutes later, Azaz capitalised on a defensive mistake to calmly slot home the second, before running straight towards the visiting supporters and making a sarcastic crying gesture, sparking a heated reaction.

This is not a rivalry that is going anywhere any time soon.

Southampton's Finn Azaz speaking to Sky Sports:

"They sang about my family home and away last season, so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back.

Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert in his press conference

Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert admitted he "didn't like" a social media video posted by the club ahead of the first meeting with Middlesbrough since 'Spygate' last season.

The video included footage of Oli McBurnie's Championship play-off final winner for Hull against Boro at Wembley in May.

It was also played on the big screens at St Mary's in the lead-up to kick-off.

"I didn't like the video this morning. No, I didn't like it," Eckert said in his post-match press conference.

"I haven't even seen the video, I've just heard the information about what was in there and I didn't like it.

"I think, if we look back a couple of months, the reality is that both clubs have lost. One club has lost off the pitch, the other has lost off the pitch. I think it's an episode that is good to close for both clubs and to move forward.

"I've apologised to Kim, I've apologised openly. For me, there is no need to warm that up again."

It was pointed out to Eckert that a box of tissues had been placed on the table behind which managers sit, seemingly mocking Hellberg after his emotional reaction to the defeat in the play-off semi-final at St Mary's in May.

After a few seconds of looking at the box, he said: "You can take this one [box of tissues] off." He then placed them under the table.

"I just love to talk about football and I hope everyone who came here, especially the Middlesbrough staff and players know that," he said.

"I hope they know these things don't come from me."

Hellberg said: "They are always trying to fire everything up. I saw there were some posts at the end where they tried to mock me - or whoever they were trying to mock - so I feel a little bit small about that.

"Otherwise, there's a very good football side, so many good players, the staff are good. There's no need for that, but it is what it is."

#740. How Hunting Wives Season 2 Killed Off 11 Characters

Hunting Wives returned to Netflix with a bang, killing off 11 characters—including season one fan-favorite Brad, played by George Ferrier—in many shocking deaths across the Netflix series' season two.

Content warning: This story contains major spoilers for Hunting Wives season two.

For the residents of Maple Brook, Texas, no character is ever really safe, as evidenced by Hunting Wives' 11 shocking deaths in season two.

The Netflix series starring Brittany Snow and Malin Akerman returned on a morbid note Nov. 26: another young girl was murdered by a predator in town. Elly was the granddaughter of gang leader Zelda Moffitt, played by Widow's Bay star Dale Dickey.

As Zelda and her biker crew, including her nephew Gentle John Moffitt (played by Cam Gigandet), investigated the killing to get payback, the trail led them to Margo's brother Kyle. To draw Kyle out, Zelda's gang kidnapped Sophie (Snow) and Margo (Akerman), during which Sophie eventually admits Kyle's been a goner since season one.

The revelation accidentally outed Gentle John as Elly's real killer, and with that mind, Zelda repaid the betrayal with an eye for an eye by fatally shooting Gigandet’s character. Unfortunately for the leader of the gang, she and four of her henchmen are offed during a tense shootout with the police when confronted during the kidnapping.

But the body count doesn't stop there. After Brad—played by George Ferrier—confronted the abuse he endured from his late mother, Jill, the trauma release caused him to bring a violent end to his final abuser, a shady music manager portrayed by John Stamos.

After killing Stamos in his luxury mansion and then shooting his father, Reverend Clint, Brad sought out his former flame, Margo, over what really happened to his ex, Abby Jackson. After the athlete figured out that the housewife was Abby's killer all along, Margo made the snap decision to silence Brad for good.

That said, hiding Margo's secret resulted in several more deaths. Her husband Jed's new campaign advisor, Lincoln Trout, orchestrated a hit on Jed's former political strategist, Jia-Yi, to protect his governorship campaign from further scandal. And in the season finale, Margo and Sophie teamed up one last time to murder television producer Nadia Kelly (Kim Matula) at the scene of a car crash after the reporter had put together that Jill was framed for Abby's murder.

Fortunately, some Maple Brook residents lived to see another day. Despite being shot by his son, Reverend Clint survived the attack, while Deputy Wanda Salazar (Karen Rodriguez) and Deputy Walter Flynn (Hunt Emery) carry on their romance thanks to Flynn coming out of his coma following the shootout with Zelda.

And Hunting Wives isn't the only series to say surprising goodbyes to fan-favorite characters. Read on for more jaw-dropping exits from hit TV shows.

Gregg Sulkin, Wizards Beyond Waverly Place

In the Wizards of Waverly Place spinoff's shocking series finale, Selena Gomez's Alex Russo reunited with teen love Mason Greyback (Sulkin)—only to reveal a devastating twist.

Greyback revealed his character died during the August 2026 episode, then his ghost filled in the gaps on what Alex has been up to in the years since his passing.

"You have a whole other life, Alex," he told her. "You got married. You have a beautiful daughter. And she needs you. That’s the life that you’re meant to live. You have to go back."

The couple announced that the third season of The Valley will be their last following a tumultuous season during which Danny’s drinking habits were questioned and he was accused of acting inappropriately while drinking.

“We’re incredibly grateful for this experience,” Danny and Nia—who share son Asher, 4, twins Isabelle and Zariah, 3, and Adelaide, 15 months—wrote in their September 2026 statement shared to social media, “but our priority is protecting our peace and our family. We are fully committed to each other and our beautiful children.”

The OneChicago fanbase was shocked when news broke in July 2026 that Miñoso, who has portrayed firefighter Joe Cruz since the show debuted in 2012, would be leaving the NBC drama during its upcoming 15th season.

The world of fire and ice featured another gruesome casualty as Ser Criston Cole was killed in the Riverlands during the Game of Thrones spinoff's July 26, 2026, episode.

In July 2026, E! News learned that Hawkins—who has portrayed Officer Kevin Atwater since the NBC drama debuted in 2014—was leaving the show after 13 seasons.

The "It's Not Unusual" singer claimed he was fired from his coaching position after 13 seasons over "financial difficulty with insurance."

“To be clear, I did not want to leave The Voice as l love the show and really appreciate the audience. ITV made this decision—obviously a while ago, and I was told just recently," Jones wrote on Instagram in September 2026. "They are offering a much-reduced role where I would make an appearance but without being actually involved from the start, and I’m not thrilled about that."

E! News confirmed in July 2026 that Scott—who has portrayed Detective Vincent Riley since the the long-running NBC crime drama's 23rd season—would leave during show's upcoming 26th season.

The Paramount+ drama's season 19 finale, released July 23, confirmed the longtime star will not be returning for season 20 after his character Elias Voit was locked up in prison for a murder he took the blame for.

"It was hard to say goodbye," Gilford told Us Weekly of his exit. "It definitely was one of my favorite characters I’ve ever gotten to play and partially because what a gift. Every season I got to do a different side of this character. It wasn’t like I was just doing the same thing every year."

Days after West Wilson confirmed his Summer House exit, news broke that Amanda, who has been a main cast member of the Bravo series since season two, will also not be returning for season 11 amid the fallout from their bombshell romance.

After his secret love affair with Amanda Batula nearly destroyed the cast friend group dynamic following season 10, it was no shocker that West walked away from the scandal (and the series) in June 2026 just weeks before season 11 was set to start filming.

The Rookie's corrupt lawyer Monica Stevens was no novice when it came to escaping death. "She's escaped multiple assassinations," actress Bridget Regan recounted to TV Insider of her character's four-season journey, "and prison time and being thrown in a woodchipper."

So when the attorney met her end on an April 2026 episode, "I wasn’t surprised," Regan noted. "I thought, 'Fair enough.' She’s had an amazing run, four years on this show. I’m only filled with gratitude."

Whitney Leavitt, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives

After making her big break on Dancing With the Stars and landing a starring role in Chicago and Broadway, the Utah native announced season five of the hit Hulu reality show will be her last as she's moving on to other professional projects.

Dr. Samira Mohan is checking out of The Pitt. Actress Supriya Ganesh will not be returning for season three of the HBO Max drama, Variety reported in April.

The exit isn't so shocking to fans given that Ganesh's character has been planning to take on a new residency program at another medical center.

The crime procedural said goodbye to Director Leon Vance (played by Rocky Carroll) in a March 2026 episode, 18 years after the leader's debut in season five. During the 500th episode, Vance was killed in a shooting with a corrupt agent and welcomed to heaven by late Chief Medical Examiner Donald "Ducky" Mallard (played by Adam Campbell).

Mehcad Brooks shocked fans in 2025 when it was revealed he was leaving the NBC crime drama ahead of season 25.

Brooks, who joined the show in 2022, portrayed Detective Jalen Shaw for three seasons.

Kevin McKidd and Kim Raver, who have played Dr. Owen Hunt and Dr. Teddy Altman respectively for nearly 20 years, shocked fans with news that they are leaving the medical drama, with their final episode being the season 22 finale May 7, 2026.

Jenna Lyons, The Real Housewives of New York City

Jenna Lyons announced she will not be returning for The Real Housewives of New York City's 16th season.

"The rumors …..Are true," the former J. Crew Creative Director wrote on Instagram in November 2025. "I was grateful to be asked to join season 16 of RHONY 'as a friend of '- knowing my personal life was not really available to be filmed, we agreed that made sense."

The fashion icon—who joined the Bravo series for season 14 in 2022—explained that she later realized being a supporting castmember wasn't for her.

"And after thinking it through I have made the difficult decision not return to the show," she continued. "I would be the oldest and only openly gay woman on the show and feel like this is an opportunity for a new dynamic to emerge."

After nine seasons, the A-list realtor is done selling mega-mansions on the Netflix reality show.

“I’ve gotten to a place where I don’t need the show financially,” Chrishell announed in November via social media. “I’m lucky to have other forms of employment, because it’s no longer good for my mental health.”

Jax Taylor announced he will not be returning to The Valley for season three amid growing concern from fans about his behavior during the show’s second season.

“Right now, my focus needs to be on my sobriety, my mental health, and coparenting," the Bravo star—who is embroiled in a nasty divorce from estranged wife Brittany Cartwright—shared in July 2025. "Taking this time is necessary for me to become the best version of myself—especially for our son, Cruz.”

Michael Longfellow, Emil Wakim & Devon Walker, Saturday Night Live

The Saturday Night Live stars all announced within days of each other that they would not be returning for the sketch comedy series' 51st season.

Longfellow and Walker each spent three seasons on SNL while Wakim exited after just one season.

Heidi Gardner & Ego Nwodim, Saturday Night Live

Weeks after Longfellow, Walker and Wakim left SNL, longtime fan-favorites Gardner and Nwodim also confirmed they would not be returning for season 51 after eight and seven seasons, respectively.

Sofia Mattsson exited the long-running soap opera in summer 2025 after seven years playing Sasha Gilmore. Her character left Port Charles for Paris.

The Pitt star Tracy Ifeachor walked away from the hit HBO Max series after the medical drama's breakout first season.

"It was an absolute privilege to play Dr. Heather Collins in such a groundbreaking season and piece," the actress posted on Instagram July 10. "Thank you to everyone who has watched & supported Season 1 & shared their stories with me."

While fans maybe should have been aware that the days were numbered for Pedro Pascal's Joel Miller, considering his April 2025 death was quite similar to how it unfolded in The Last of Us Part II, the 2020 video game season two of The Last of Us is based on, the moment his character was brutally impaled still stunned.

Pascal, meanwhile, who also died onscreen in Game of Thrones and Buffy the Vampire Slayer, took his game over status in stride. "I get killed a lot," he joked to Entertainment Weekly. "I like to die."

After what he dubbed "one wild adventure," Peter Krause officially extinguished his role as 9-1-1's Los Angeles Fire Department captain Bobby Nash on an April 2025 episode of the procedural drama.

“Bobby Nash was written in sacrifice, and he was built for this,” Krause wrote in a statement to the Hollywood Reporter. “First responders risk their lives on the job so that others can see another day. His story arc honors them.”

Killing off the somewhat tormented, but beloved, firefighter was certainly a hot topic, showrunner Tim Minear acknowledged to Variety, "but after eight years, it just felt like, if we have any hope of creating stories going forward that have actual stakes, then someone's got to die."

Paige DeSorbo announced in June 2025 that she was walking away from the Bravo series after seven seasons.

"You’ve seen me grow up over these last 7 summers. I’ll always be grateful for the memories, the community, and the opportunities this wild ride has brought me," the Giggly Squad podcast cohost shared with fans on Instagram. "But like all good things (and some bad decisions), it’s time for this chapter to close."

The French actress confirmed she would not return for the hit Netflix series' fifth season in April 2025.

"After an incredible journey, I’ve made the decision to step away from Emily in Paris,” she wrote in an April 23 Instagram post, alongside pictures of her and her former castmates on set. “It has been a truly wonderful experience, one filled with growth, creativity, and unforgettable memories.”

Ahead of The Sex Lives of College Girls' third season, Reneé Rapp announced she would be leaving the Max series.

"College Girls moved me out to LA and introduced me to some of my favorite people," she wrote on social media in July 2023. "2 and a half years later—it's given me y'all and this community."

The show's co-creator Mindy Kaling also confirmed Rapp's exit. "We love @reneerapp so much and of course will be so sad to say goodbye to Leighton Murray!" Kaling wrote on her Instagram Stories before referencing Rapp's thriving music career. "We can't wait to see our friend on tour!!"

More than a year after Kevin Costner was rumored to have unexpectedly walked away from the hit Paramount drama after four and a half seasons, he confirmed in June 2024 that he will not return to finish out the series' fifth and final season.

After 19 years as Meredith Grey, Ellen Pompeo scrubbed in for the last time as a series regular on the ABC drama in February 2023.

"I gotta mix it up a little bit," Pompeo explained on The Drew Barrymore Show in December 2022, though she has already returned for a May guest appearance and continues narrating the series. "I'm 53, my brain is like scrambled eggs. I gotta do something new. You can't do The New York Times crossword puzzle every single day."

But she's not gone for good. Pompeo still pops in and out of Grey Sloan Memorial Hospital.

#739. Celtic defend head of security amid Green Brigade row

The Green Brigade occupy a standing section at Celtic Park

Celtic have defended their head of security and the action taken against the Green Brigade last season after the fan group declared four supporters had been cleared over the incident that sparked a lengthy ban.

A Green Brigade statement said the four had been "finally cleared of wrongdoing" over the occurrence, which took place during a game against Falkirk on 29 October last year.

The Scottish champions released footage at the time which they said showed "around 100" supporters verbally abusing and assaulting a steward and two police officers.

The alleged flashpoint came after a ticket inspection at the rail seating section of Celtic Park, the club explained, as they outlined a ban on about 250 supporters, which lasted nearly six months.

The Green Brigade say Celtic's "irresponsible and vindictive claim" was intended to "smear" them.

A statement from the group said: "Not guilty pleas were accepted by both Procurator Fiscal and sheriff for breach of the peace charges before the trial commenced.

"The four supporters cleared were subjected to dawn raids, damage to homes and harassment of family members including confiscation of personal devices, this included a vulnerable adult who was left alone in the cold with no means to contact anyone after the front door was removed."

Celtic lift suspension of Green Brigade fans group

The Green Brigade called for the club to apologise for the collective ban and to lift suspensions on two supporters who remain banned over their interaction with head of security Mark Hargreaves at last year's abandoned annual general meeting.

"This week's outcome represents significant vindication for all supporters concerned in these events over the past year," they added.

"It also calls into question the credibility of Mark Hargreaves' subsequent allegations against two Green Brigade representatives."

Celtic pointed out they play no part in criminal proceedings and added that they were not aware all had been completed. And they stated that the outcome of the four cases did not alter their assessment of the incident.

The club said: "The conduct of the group witnessed that day was unsafe and completely unacceptable â it has no place at Celtic Park or anywhere in football. The club took reasonable and proportionate steps to deal with this conduct.

"Such was the seriousness of the incident that the club was called to attend a special meeting of the Safety Advisory Group of Glasgow City Council."

Celtic accused the Green Brigade of continuing a "campaign of personal harassment and abuse" towards former senior police officer Hargreaves.

"Mark is a highly-qualified, dedicated professional who plays a crucial role at the club in ensuring the safety of our supporters.

"Where conduct presents an unacceptable risk to that safety or demonstrates an unwillingness to co-operate with it, the club has to take appropriate and proportionate action."

BBC Scotland have contacted Police Scotland for comment.

Black Friday is the huge annual shopping event that takes place the day after Thanksgiving in the United States, and it’s considered the official kickoff to the holiday shopping season. #737. Forest beat Chelsea to heap pressure on Alonso as Fofana is booed

Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea. Premier League.

The City GroundAttendance: Attendance30,851.

Report and free match highlights as Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea 3-2 at The City Ground; Igor Jesus opened the scoring before Morgan Gibbs-White scored two. Emmanuel Emegha's brace in vain; Wesley Fofana was booed by the Chelsea supporters

Football Features Writer @ghostgoal

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Morgan Gibbs-White scored two in Nottingham Forest’s 3-2 win over Chelsea at the City Ground as the crisis deepened for Xabi Alonso.

Igor Jesus volleyed Forest in front inside five minutes of what was a dismal first half for Chelsea and they never recovered parity. Wesley Fofana - booed by his own supporters throughout - conceded a penalty early in the second half that Gibbs-White converted.

Emmanuel Emegha did come off the bench to pull one back soon afterwards but another goal from the Forest captain better reflected the superiority of Oliver Glasner's side even if Emegha's second in the 89th minute made for a surprisingly nervy finale.

Forest began the evening beside the Trent with only goal difference keeping them out of the relegation zone, but victory lifts them clear of the bottom six. The spotlight now falls on Chelsea, who missed the chance to climb back into the top five.

It is four Premier League defeats in their last five games under Alonso who appears to be scrambling for solutions given the evidence of this team selection. It is not only Fofana under scrutiny at Chelsea. A club in disarray? Alonso needs to get a grip on it and fast.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Liam Delap had been the two-goal hero in the 3-1 win over Manchester City last time out at home and would have been desperate to score against another of his former clubs but it was Igor Jesus' stunning strike that silenced the Chelsea supporters early on.

"It is the first opportunity for them to play together, they have different strengths," Glasner had told Sky Sports beforehand. Igor Jesus' strengths include volleys beyond Emiliano Martinez, it turns out. It was his first goal at the City Ground since April.

Alonso had responded to the alarming defeat to Leeds by dropping Levi Colwill and playing Moises Caicedo in defence. The Chelsea boss changed to a back four as well in a bid to find some form after losing three of their previous four Premier League games.

"Today we need strong characters, big personalities," said Alonso beforehand. "Players that know what it takes to compete in the Premier League." That explained the decision to bring in Danny Welbeck up front, with Jordan Henderson holding midfield together.

But Welbeck was a passenger in the first half, having only seven touches of the ball - half as many as anyone else - while Henderson found himself overrun. Forest were at the back line time and again. Chelsea were fortunate to be only one down at the break.

Fofana had not endeared himself to supporters by giving an unauthorised interview in which he not only talked of being close to quitting football but appeared to joke about missing a penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool. This performance was worse.

He was culpable for Forest's second goal, bested by Delap before hastily fouling him inside the penalty box in a rash attempt to recover. Gibbs-White slotted home from the spot and Fofana was substituted to the sound obscene chants from the Chelsea fans.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Alonso's side did pull one back through the young substitute Emegha, when Pedro Neto's shot was deflected kindly into his path. But Xaver Schlager's sumptuous ball clipped in behind the Chelsea defence allowed Gibbs-White to hook home his second.

Emegha nodded in another late on to make the decision to omit him after scoring the first goal against Leeds look even more of an error, but it was not enough to earn an undeserved point. Forest held on and are on the up again. Chelsea have problems.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner speaking in the press conference:

"It looks like we are progressing and this is what we all want to see. But also last time [against Man City] was the first swallow [that does not make a summer] and now it's the second swallow and I think everybody could feel it tonight.

"So stay humble, take this feeling of the win and the confidence and the belief but stay humble and prepare well for the three-game week before we face Brighton here.

"We are all feeling again that we are heading in the right direction. Still a lot to do, but every win helps in building confidence and trust. But still 12 points after 12 games is not enough."

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso speaking in the press conference:

"We are working, trying to find solutions, trying to do our best, but things are not going the way we want. And I don't understand any other way but to work, to try again.

"Because if we want to get something, it will have to come from us. No one will come from outside to give us a solution. And the quality that we need, the mentality that we need, it needs to come from within the team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"Overall, we can do better. I think that we are going through a difficult moment of confidence, things are not clicking, things are not going the way we want.

"We know that in football, this can change quickly, or this can continue. So it's down to us to work and to find solutions to have a better feeling on the pitch and to get better results, because that's what we need."

Asked if he was frustrated with the Chelsea fans booing Wesley Fofana:

"We need to support everyone because we need everyone. We need the fans, we need all the players, we need to stick together, because if not, it will get more complicated."

#735. Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs, citing ongoing losses — reports

According to a letter obtained by the media, Lufthansa's executive board said the German company is losing €20 million every month. In addition to job cuts, operational cuts are also planned.

Germany's flagship airline Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 jobs at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs, according to a company letter seen by German news agency DPA and news outlets.

The letter was reportedly signed by Lufthansa CEO Jens Ritter and four other board members.

This is reportedly down to ongoing financial losses. In the first nine months of the year, the airline recorded an operating loss of €180 million ($197 million).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The executive board said on average the loss amounts to €20 million every month, according to media reports. The board stated in the letter that "this is the third year in a row of not being financially successful."

"Lufthansa is currently not competitive in terms of its cost structure, efficiency and productivity," the letter said.

At the end of 2025, the Lufthansa group employed some 67,100 people, up 1% from the previous year.

The company also plans to cut employee travel benefits, restructure its hub operations to reduce crew overnight stays abroad, and reduce short- and medium-haul capacity by replacing some A320 aircraft with A220 jets.

Furthermore, it plans to equip ten aircraft per month with Starlink, a satellite internet service developed by tech billionaire Elon Musk. The airline hopes to generate "additional revenue” by monetizing onboard internet access, according to the letter.

The time frame of the cuts is unclear. It's also unknown whether the cuts were a part of a previously announced downsizing.

In September 2025, Lufthansa said it would slash 4,000 administrative positions due to the implementation of AI and digitalization.

In regards to this year, Lufthansa has faced rising fuel costs spurred by the US-Israeli war with Iran, further complicating its financial outlook.

#734. What went wrong for Alonso's Chelsea at Forest?

Sky Sports analyses the decisions from Xabi Alonso that contributed to Chelsea's 3-2 defeat to Nottingham Forest; Wesley Fofana started despite his controversial interview, while Levi Colwill was dropped; Xabi Alonso called for fundamentals but Chelsea were outrun

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Xabi Alonso called for his Chelsea side to get back to the fundamentals before kick-off - and then watched on as they were outworked and outclassed on their way to a miserable 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest.

"Everyone in the club and team, we need to stick together and go through this moment. We have to deal with it and we are responsible," Alonso told Sky Sports after the game, which marked their third successive defeat in the Premier League.

"It is a difficult moment for everyone at the club. For the team and the fans. Disappointed to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions.

"We can't stop. We are low in confidence. At this level you need to hold results and not concede so much. That is why we are losing."

Alonso now has as many losses in 15 games across all competitions as he did in 34 for Real Madrid (6). Since March, no side has more defeats in the top-flight than the Blues (14). And their problems are mounting by the day.

Here, Sky Sports analyses the decisions that contributed to the worrying defeat at the City Ground.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Despite the calls from Alonso to strip the game back to basics and get the fundamentals right, Chelsea felt short from minute one.

At the half-time interval, facing a 1-0 deficit and with zero shots on target, Chelsea had ran 3.8km less than Oliver Glasner's side.

The Forest boss was then quick to point out that they had outrun their opponents by 6km after the game. Yes, Chelsea had more possession, but they were also well behind in high-speed runs.

"I've seen one team jogging after the ball and one team sprinting after the ball and in this day and age, you cannot do that," said Jamie Redknapp.

"Distance covered is not always the barometer, but one thing is for sure, high-speed runs will tell you everything."

Starting Wesley Fofana in the same week the player had to apologise for his controversial interview, where he said he can "laugh about" the penalty miss that contributed to their Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool and contemplated retirement during injury spells at the club, was a bold move from Alonso. It did not pay off.

The tone was set early on. Fofana's first touches were heavily booed by the travelling Chelsea fans who had made the 130-mile journey in the cold and rain to watch their side slip to yet another dismal defeat.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

The centre-back could only watch on as Igor Jesus volleyed in his stunning opener but was at the centre of attention, for all the wrong reasons, for the second.

After misjudging the ball while battling with former teammate Liam Delap, who caused problems all evening, Fofana rushed to atone for his error and fouled the striker in the penalty area.

Morgan Gibbs-White doubled the lead from the spot and ultimately the comeback, led by substitute Emmanuel Emegha, fell short.

He was cautioned for the challenge and eventually taken off for Levi Colwill, who was dropped by Alonso instead of Fofana, and the fans booed him once again.

"It didn't feel like a game for him tonight. He had a bad week with the podcast," said Jamie Redknapp after the game.

"By playing Fofana tonight, you created that. It was inevitable. He is lacking so much confidence; he needs some time.

"He is having a real difficult run of it at the moment."

After making the decision to drop Colwill, options at the centre of defence were limited with Maxence Lacroix and Reece James both sidelined.

Playing Josh Acheampong at centre-back and giving a rare start to Malo Gusto, an unused substitute on the night, seemed the more obvious choice but Alonso opted to play Moises Caicedo, arguably the best midfielder in the league, in the back four instead.

He was then tasked with dealing with a strike partnership of Delap and Igor Jesus. A difficult task for even the tallest of centre-backs, let alone a makeshift one standing at 5-foot-10.

He gave space to the Brazil striker for the opener and his presence in midfield was missed. He still led the way with 114 passes on the night, but Chelsea needed him in the middle of the park to deal with the likes of James McAtee and Xaver Schlager.

"They have bought players but if they do not sign a centre back, they cannot compete," said Redknapp after the game. He is right.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Alonso admitted that Emegha's performance after scoring twice off the bench was the lone positive for his side to take from their trip to the East Midlands. "For sure, he is having a good impact," he said. "He has done well. That is a positive."

He scored his first goal in the 4-1 defeat to Leeds United last time out but lost his place in the starting line-up on Friday.

Danny Welbeck, 36, was given the nod ahead of him and his performance mirrored the struggles Chelsea had as a unit.

Alonso called on the experience of Jordan Henderson and Welbeck to help weather their current struggles but it only whipped up the storm.

Welbeck was a bystander in the first half and had just seven touches before being replaced at the break, Emegha then scored with his first two to help spark hopes of a comeback.

His header for the second, holding off Jair Cunha, was one of the rare moments Chelsea matched the physicality of their opponents. He has to start moving forward without Joao Pedro available.

Alonso said the only way he knows how to address these issues is to attack them on the training ground. He has just five days to do that before they are put to the test against Crystal Palace, live on Sky Sports, who will be desperate for a win.

#732. Head coach Slegers leaves Arsenal 18 months after Champions League win

Renee Slegers initially joined Arsenal in 2023 as an assistant coach under Jonas Eidevall

Arsenal have parted company with head coach Renee Slegers by mutual consent after a disappointing start to the season.

Slegers, 37, was initially appointed on an interim basis in October 2024 before being handed the role permanently three months later.

The Dutchwoman led Arsenal to their second Women's Champions League title in May 2025 and the inaugural Fifa Women's Champions Cup in February 2026.

But she leaves with the team sixth in the Women's Super League after 11 matches - 12 points behind leaders Chelsea.

Assistant coach Aaron D'Antino has also left the club, with assistant Melissa Clarke-Reed placed in interim charge as they begin the search for a permanent replacement.

D'Antino had been part of Arsenal's coaching staff since August 2018.

Arsenal director of women's football Clare Wheatley said the decision had been "extremely difficult".

"In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural Fifa Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron," she said.

"After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary."

Chief executive Richard Garlick paid tribute to both departing coaches, describing Slegers as "a wonderful person" who had played "an integral role in some of the most historic achievements in the club's history".

"Our ambition is to compete for and win major trophies consistently, and our recent results have led us to conclude that a change is necessary to give us the best opportunity to achieve those goals," he added.

Why Arsenal are behind in race for Champions League spots

Slegers' departure comes after weeks of pressure as Arsenal's WSL form continued to deteriorate.

While the Dutch coach delivered the Women's Champions League and Women's Champions Cup, results in the league have fallen below expectations this season.

Arsenal have endured a four-match winless run in the league and their struggles have been particularly stark at their own Emirates Stadium, where they have gone six matches without a victory.

For a side expected to challenge for major trophies every season, those dropped points are damaging as they have fallen well adrift of Chelsea and even eight points behind London City Lionesses, who are in the third Women's Champions League qualification spot.

A lack of goals has been central to Arsenal's struggles. They have scored just 11 times in 11 WSL matches this season - less than half the tally of Chelsea (29), second-placed Manchester City (28) and London City Lionesses (31).

Before Slegers' exit was confirmed on Friday, former Arsenal and England forward Lianne Sanderson had called for the manager to depart.

"I've been a big advocate for Renee to stay in the job, but after the Lyon game [a 2-0 home defeat in the Champions League], I felt this feeling in my stomach that it's time [to part ways]," Sanderson told FourFourTwo, external.

"That was probably the most defeated I have felt. The players weren't fighting, they had just shown nothing, there was no identity.

"The definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results."

After Sunday's draw with West Ham, Slegers acknowledged performances and results had fallen short of expectations and made it clear she accepted responsibility.

"I love the club," she said. "We're going through a very, very difficult time, and I take my responsibilities, because the results haven't been good enough.

"In the second half we are chasing again, but we're not creating good enough chances to the final third, from all phases, and the way we get there, it's not the Arsenal standard and we need to do that better.

"But I take my responsibilities in my role."

#730. FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?

Two challengers to Gianni Infantino have registered for next year's FIFA presidential election. What do Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima stand for – and do they stand a chance against the incumbent?

Three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027. DW looks at the field of candidates.

Gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era. Under Infantino's leadership, FIFA's revenues have continued to grow, the Club World Cup has been revamped, and the men's World Cup has been expanded to include 48 teams.

During his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support. Infantino enjoys significant backing in Africa, South America, and large parts of Asia — a result of multi-billion-dollar development programs and financial grants provided to national associations. Many smaller member associations view him as a president who takes their interests more seriously than his predecessors did.

At the same time, critics accuse Infantino of consolidating power within the organization around himself. During his tenure, oversight and control bodies have been restructured multiple times, and key positions have been filled with his own loyalists.

Infantino's ostentatious closeness to political leaders has also sparked debate — whether exemplified by his conduct during the World Cup in Qatar, his tight ties to Saudi Arabia or his public appearances alongside US President Donald Trump (though that relationship is said to have cooled significantly after the 2026 World Cup). Detractors accuse him of seeking proximity to authoritarian rulers and intermingling political interests too closely with football.

A failed initiative to grant private investors a larger stake in lucrative FIFA competitions (FIFA Forward Enterprise) has also placed Infantino under considerable pressure. As the FIFA election approaches, he faces the prospect of legal challenges; European football's governing body UEFA is aiming to take action over the investment plan, while other critics are calling for an investigation by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

However, his time in office has brought many of FIFA's 211 member associations additional development funding and other revenue. This makes him the man to beat in the March vote.

Philippe Diallo is Europe's candidate. The 63-year-old, who was elected president of the French Football Federation in 2023, is seen as an experienced sports administrator with a pragmatic and measured leadership style.

He has the backing of UEFA, as well as many of its 55 member associations, including the German Football Association (DEB).

"Philippe Diallo stands for a version of football that embraces responsibility and tackles future challenges with determination," DFB President Bernd Neuendorf said in a statement announcing the German FA's position.

"We want a FIFA that serves the sport in the interest of all its member associations. That is why we support Philippe Diallo with great conviction."

Diallo is positioning himself as a clear alternative to Infantino. His supporters see him as a candidate who stands for sound leadership, transparency, and a stronger dialogue with member associations. Unlike the incumbent, however, he lacks a global network of allies.

The third man in the race is Kozo Tashima. The 68-year-old was president of the Japan Football Association (JFA) from 2016 to 2024 and has been one of the most influential officials in Asia for decades.

During a press conference in the Japanese capital Tokyo on Friday, Tashima mentioned the words "integrity, fairness, trust and transparency" several times in explaining his decision to run.

"I just don't only want to be the FIFA president, my intention is to make FIFA better," he said.

"Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organization."

Tashima also acknowledged that failing to have won the endorsement of any of the regional confederations — the Asian Football Confederation is supporting Infantino — makes him a longshot to win the election.

But he could still play a key role in the outcome. At a press conference on Tuesday, Diallo said he intended to reach out to Tashima to "unite forces" to defeat Infantino. Tashima hasn't ruled out the notion.

"We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he's a great person to team up with," he said.

"Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management," he added.

However, Tashima also noted that he hadn't had any thoughts of withdrawing from the race.

If Infantino's challengers do manage to join forces in some way, they might just stand a chance of upsetting the highly favored incumbent.

Lyon, a mainstay for the Baggy Greens for 13 years, has not spoken publicly since Usman Khawaja's explosive Sandpapergate claims were published in his autobiography.

Australia selection chair George Bailey confirmed that the 39-year-old's omission for a series that starts in Perth on December 9 was not related to the ongoing saga but based on performances.

Pat Cummins (captain), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Jack Clayton, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Michael Neser, Matt Renshaw, Corey Rocchiccioli, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc.

#727. Price out in Players Championship Finals first round in night of upsets

Report as Grand Slam champion Gerwyn Price, World No 2 Gian Van Veen, and No 1 seed Wessel Nijman all knocked out in first round at Players Championship Finals; watch the World Darts Championship at London's Alexandra Palace, live on Sky Sports from December 11-January 3

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Three of darts' biggest names were subject to shock upsets in the Players Championship Finals as Grand Slam champion Gerwyn Price, World No 2 Gian Van Veen, and No 1 seed Wessel Nijman were all knocked out in the first round at Minehead.

Price was beaten by 6-4 Sebastian Bialecki - the first time the Pole had beaten the Welshman in his career - while Jeffery de Graaf won two legs on the bounce to consign van Veen to defeat by the same scoreline.

Nijman was upset by 20-year-old Henry Coates despite posting an average of 110 - the second-highest average in Players Championship Finals history.

World No 4 Luke Humphries, meanwhile, battled through his recurring back injury to secure a routine 6-3 victory against Darryl Pilgrim, while Michael van Gerwen withstood Connor Scutt to secure safe passage with a 6-3 first-round win of his own.

Beau Greaves also progressed to the second round with a scrappy 6-3 victory against former Lakeside champion Christian Kist despite a mediocre average of 89.64, and will face Rob Owen in the next round.

Van Veen, Nijman and Price joined James Wade, Gary Anderson, and Rob Cross as six of the top 25 players in the world were eliminated at the first opportunity in the last major before the World Darts Championship, which is live on Sky Sports from December 11th.

Wade was beaten 6-4 by Justin Hood and 2014 winner Anderson slipped to a 6-4 loss against Karel Sedlacek, while Cross fell to a thrilling 6-5 loss to Mickey Mansell.

Van Veen - who finished runner-up to Price at the Grand Slam - struggled from the outset and throughout his match, managing only one maximum and checking out a lowly 15% of his finishes.

The Dutchman had three darts at double 16 to keep himself in the tournament, but failed to level the scores at 5-5 before de Graaf ruthlessly produced a 112 checkout to produce the first upset of the round.

Price, fresh off his first major win in four years after three successive final defeats, was heavily favoured against 22-year-old Bialecki, and looked to have rediscovered his tournament-winning form at the perfect moment when he produced a stunning 120 checkout to peg the deficit back to 5-4.

But Bialecki kept his cool and threw for the match, claiming his first career win against Price at the seventh attempt. The Pole will face off against de Graaf in round two.

The status quo was somewhat restored when Humphries and van Gerwen produced characteristically routine wins against lower-ranked opponents, with Humphries silencing doubters by averaging 93.32 in a week dominated by coverage of his injury.

But the show was stolen by Coates. The Derby native overcame his opponent's stellar average by notching an incredible 85.71% checkout success rate to claim victory in only his fourth-ever televised game.

Elsewhere, Stephen Bunting edged into the next round after beating German Max Hopp in a last-leg decider, while Kevin Doets averaged 107.34 in his win over Ritchie Edhouse and Chris Dobey came from behind to beat Mike De Decker 6-4.

#725. Chromosome ‘glue’ could boost fertility by stabilizing ageing eggs

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Chromosomes are held together with protein structures called cohesins, but these diminish with age.Credit: Power and Syred/SPL

Researchers have engineered a ‘molecular glue’ that can stabilize chromosomes in ageing mouse eggs1. They say their artificial cohesion system could pave the way for improved fertility treatments for women over the age of 35.

Chromosomes in animal eggs are held together by protein structures called cohesins. These help to ensure that chromosomes divide correctly during the process of cell division. But the level of cohesins declines as women age, which can cause chromosomes to separate early and be distributed incorrectly. The resulting eggs can have too many or too few chromosomes, a condition known as aneuploidy, which is a cause of infertility, failed in vitro fertilization (IVF) treatments and early pregnancy loss, particularly in women who are older than 35 years.

To prevent this premature separation of chromosomes in eggs, Melina Schuh, a biochemist at Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences in Göttingen, Germany, and her colleagues designed an artificial system called TALhesin. The system uses engineered proteins that attach to regions of the chromosome in which cohesin is usually present; these proteins then bind to one another.

Many groups are trying to understand cohesin because it diminishes as women age, affecting fertility, says Bettina Mihalas, a reproductive biologist at the University of New South Wales in Sydney, Australia, but this is the first approach to replace the protein’s function with an engineered system. “It’s a very creative, well-engineered and well-thought-out approach,” she says.

The findings were published in Science1 on 26 November.

The researchers injected messenger RNA that encoded the engineered proteins into immature mouse eggs. The mouse eggs then produced the proteins. Using fluorescence microscopy imaging, the researchers confirmed that the TALhesin proteins attached to chromosome regions in which natural cohesin is usually lost.

The artificial system reduced the frequency of early chromosome separation in older mice aged 13 months, 17 months and 20 months compared with untreated eggs. In 17-month-old mice, the proportion of eggs without any premature chromosome-separation errors increased from 46.7% to 74.1% in those treated with TALhesin, similar to what is observed in eggs from young mice.

Chromatids — the two identical halves formed by a replicating chromosome — must separate at the right time during cell division. To enable this, the researchers added a ‘molecular scissor’ into their artificial system. This switched off the artificial cohesion system at the appropriate time.

The team has adapted the system to deliver engineered proteins that attach to regions of human chromosomes in which cohesin is usually present.

Experiments in donated human eggs showed that the TALhesin proteins accumulated in these regions. The researchers also found that chromosomes with high levels of the engineered proteins tended to have smaller distances between chromatids. This demonstrates that the TALhesin system holds the chromosomes together.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03874-7

Webster, A. et al. Science 394, 982–989 (2026).

#724. No Rodgers, no problem! Steelers shock Broncos after dramatic week

The Pittsburgh Steelers stun the Denver Broncos 27-5 in their first game since releasing four-time MVP quarterback Aaron Rodgers following his remarkable comments regarding head coach Mike McCarthy; Rodgers had accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings

It had been a week clouded by Aaron Rodgers and his explosive claims regarding head coach Mike McCarthy, but the Pittsburgh Steelers swatted at the storm to claim a shock 27-5 win over the Super Bowl-contending Denver Broncos on Black Friday.

Broncos quarterback Bo Nix endured a miserable afternoon as he surrendered two interceptions and a lost fumble that resulted in two defensive touchdowns for the Steelers.

Denver trailed 24-5 after a dire first half in which they were limited to just 58 yards of offense, becoming just the third team since 1991 to post fewer than 60 yards while conceding two defensive touchdowns over the first two quarters of a game.

TJ Watt scored with an end zone fumble recovery, Jalen Ramsey returned a Nix interception to the house and D.K. Metcalf recorded a touchdown catch before appearing to celebrate by holding up eight fingers in an apparent support of Rodgers.

The Broncos looked anything but a contender as they slumped to 8-3, while the Steelers distanced themselves from a reflection of turmoil to improve to 7-4 in their push for the playoffs.

The Rodgers saga had lingered as an unwelcome backdrop heading into the game after the four-time MVP quarterback was released this week in the wake of his sensational appearance on the Pat McAfee Show.

Rodgers had claimed that head coach McCarthy fell asleep in team meetings, rebuffed suggestions to connect better with Pittsburgh's defensive players and accidentally shouted "one, two, three, Packers!" at the end of a team talk against the Philadelphia Eagles, the latter of which McCarthy would admit as an embarrassing moment.

Rudolph started in place of Rodgers for the first time since the incident as he went nine of 15 passing for 142 yards and a touchdown, while Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren combined for 117 yards on the ground.

Reflecting on their win after such an eventful week, Rudolph said: "We just sort of rallied around Coach McCarthy, and I think in a weird way, the adversity brought us brought us closer together.

"It was a lot. Sort of unprecedented - certainly like nothing I've ever been through, and probably the same for all of my team-mates.

"I'm just so proud of the way we turned the page from [Aaron Rodgers' release on] Wednesday, and the veteran leadership - the Cam Haywards, the Jalen Ramseys, the TJ Watts - they really led us forward."

It took until 9.23 remaining in the third quarter for the first first down of the second half to arrive when the struggling Nix connected with Jaylen Waddle for 22 yards.

Still, it would come up empty amid a sequence of five successive punts between the teams, until Denver turned the ball over when Zach Allen forced a fumble from Dowdle that was recovered by Riley Moss with 3.31 on the clock.

Such was the story of their night that Denver failed to capitalise as their resulting drive ended in Wil Lutz missing a 53-yard field goal at the beginning of the fourth quarter.

Rudolph followed up by launching a downfield strike to Roman Wilson for 37 yards to set up Chris Boswell's 33-yard field goal for a 27-5 lead with 11.16 to play.

Nix's turnover issues resumed when he was intercepted by Daylen Everette at Pittsburgh's seven-yard line to ultimately end the game.

For so long defense has been the heartbeat of the Steelers operation, and it leapt to the occasion in the opening exchanges by way of TJ Watt as their stalwart edge rusher downed Nix's finger-slip fumble in the end zone for a deadlock-breaking touchdown in the first quarter.

Pittsburgh then forced a swift three-and-out to pave the way for Rudolph's 22-yard touchdown strike to Metcalf, who did outstandingly to haul in a back-pedalling catch while facing man coverage from star corner Pat Surtain II.

Denver turned to their own defense as a potential route back into the game when Alex Singleton stuffed Warren in the end zone for a safety, before Lutz and Boswell exchanged a pair of 44 and 47-yard field goals.

The Steelers then stretched their lead with a second defensive first-half touchdown when Ramsey turned a Nix interception into a 36-yard slaloming pick-six with 1.33 to play.

#722. Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV

In the latest in a series of raids and arrests, another major pro-opposition Turkish broadcaster has been brought under state control. This is the third in a year.

Another important opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control. On Tuesday morning, authorities raided the offices of the television broadcaster Sozcu TV and the news portal Sozcu.com.tr, and arrested several executives.

A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge. Sozcu was one of the last big media companies in Turkey to regularly report critically on the government of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices. According to Sozcu, its chairwoman, Funda Tuncer Sidali, and Asim Akgul, the former chief executive of the Sozcu group, were among those arrested.

The broadcaster did not initially announce the appointment of the trustee on its digital channels. It did call on its audience to follow it under a new account. The leader of the main opposition party, Ozgur Ozel, declared on X: "You will never be able to prevent this nation's voice from rising, its rebellion from being heard, its cry from echoing."

The Istanbul public prosecutor's office has confirmed the arrangements. It justified the investigation with claims of a suspected connection between the owner of Sozcu, Burak Akhay, and the Gülen movement. The Turkish government blames this movement, which was once allied to Erdogan, for the attempted coup in 2016, and has designated it a terrorist organization.

According to the investigators, Akbay is said to have used foreign bank accounts to finance two companies involved in media activities on behalf of the Gülen movement. They claim there is strong suspicion that he was able, in this way, to hold a leadership position in the organization.

It is not new for the Turkish state to take over media organizations by appointing trustees. Many media companies accused of being close to the Gülen movement were brought under state control in this way after the attempted coup in 2016. What is new is that for about a year now this is also happening to media seen as pro-opposition.

Sozcu is not the first opposition broadcaster to be targeted by the authorities. The TELEI TV channel was searched on October 24, 2025. Its editor-in-chief, Merdan Yanardag, was arrested on charges of espionage and remains in custody. The offices of Halk TV were raided on October 14 this year. There, too, a trustee was put in charge.

In the space of just over a year, three of the most important opposition television channels have been brought under state control. Observers see this as another step toward an increasingly authoritarian and politically isolated system.

Berk Esen, a political scientist with Sabanci University in Istanbul, sees these measures as a significant weakening of the opposition in the public domain.

Esen told DW that the government may first have acted behind the scenes and tried to bring Sozcu to heel politically. When this didn't succeed, it invoked the judiciary. Esen says Turkey is increasingly moving toward an authoritarian system. The attempt to prevent opposition organizations and media from gaining strength and influence is part of this.

Esen describes the opposition's success in local government elections in March 2024 as a political turning point. Since then, he says, the government has seen its chances of winning political competitions at the ballot box receding. "It's become harder for the AKP to win elections," says Esen. "That's why it's attacking the opposition and the free media both at once."

Several opposition mayors have also been arrested in recent months and replaced by trustees. They include the mayor of Istanbul and presidential candidate Ekrem Imamoglu, who has been in detention since his arrest in March last year. He is regarded as one of Erdogan's most promising challengers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The Turkish Journalists' Association (TGC) spoke of a "black winter for press freedom," and announced its solidarity with all those affected. It described the recent developments as a serious attack on press freedom. The fact that a trustee had been appointed, first at Halk TV and now at Sozcu, showed how the media climate in Turkey has deteriorated, it said.

"These days, too, shall pass," the TGC declared. "When that day comes, those journalists who seek the truth today will be remembered, as will the decisions that prevent the public from hearing that truth."

#721. Man Utd trigger Fernandes' one-year contract extension

Bruno Fernandes joined Manchester United in 2020

Manchester United have triggered their one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract.

The 32-year-old's deal was due to expire next summer but sources say both parties decided it was in their best interests to activate the option through to 2028.

It means overseas clubs will not be able to approach Fernandes when the transfer window opens on 1 January.

The Portugal international confirmed on Tuesday that discussions over a new contract had been paused. Sources say they will resume once United's league position has improved.

Fernandes has made 343 appearances for United, scoring 115 goals, since his Â£47m move from Sporting in January 2020.

Last season he broke the Premier League assists record and scooped all of the individual player of the year awards after an outstanding campaign as United finished third.

While there is doubt over his long-term future, extending the contract means United would be able to command a fee for Fernandes should he leave in the summer.

United had been open to selling Fernandes in the summer of 2025, with Saudi Pro-League club Al Hilal offering a huge deal.

After discussing the situation with his wife, Fernandes decided to stay, though he later said it "hurt" United were willing to sell him. He reiterated on Tuesday he was still ambitious to win the biggest honours in the game.

Fernandes is a doubt for Saturday's Premier League encounter with Brentford after returning from the Champions League trip to Sporting with a virus.

The playmaker, who scored both goals in the 2-2 draw with his former club, but did not train on Friday and head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he would take a decision on his captain's fitness on Saturday morning.

"We are going to assess during the day and then tomorrow see how he is when he wakes up," said Pochettino. "We are not going to take any risks."

Pochettino is preparing for his first home game as Man Utd boss

Pochettino was criticised by former Liverpool and England midfielder Jamie Redknapp on the Overlap earlier this week.

Reference was made to the former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea coach high-fiving Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davidson after his side's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, as evidence Pochettino had lost his edge.

"When I saw Pochettino at Southampton and I saw him at Tottenham, he looked like he had that Argentinian dog in him," said Redknapp.

"I look at him now and he's high-fiving everyone, he's got the bracelets on, he's got the barnet. I think he's gone too nice."

It seems someone had mentioned the observation to Pochettino as he went off on a tangent at his Friday news conference when asked about a "crazy" first week that included red cards, refereeing errors, disallowed goals and a drone filming training.

"What are we going to do? Start to cry?" he asked. "No. We have to be strong, believe and keep going. I cannot judge the past. Who am I to do that? I was in Cincinnati. I was outside. I need to shut my mouth, say nothing and start from now.

"Sometimes we are so confusing two words that means something similar; nice and good. I am not nice. We have to be good. It is a different thing. We know when we need to push, when we need to be strong, and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything.

Pochettino also confirmed Â£70m midfielder Carlos Baleba is expected to be out until the last week in January with the hamstring injury he sustained against Roma on 3 November.

Forward Marcus Rashford had begun to do individual work outside as he tries to recover from a hip problem that has kept him out since 13 October.

#720. Billy Ray Cyrus Shares Rare Photos of Son Christopher on Thanksgiving

Billy Ray Cyrus celebrated Thanksgiving surrounded by family, including his rarely seen son Christopher Cody Cyrus, his wife Nicole and their baby Hudson.

Billy Ray Cyrus is celebrating in the heart of family.

The 65-year-old proved his heart is anything but achy breaky as he and partner Elizabethy Hurley enjoyed a blended Thanksgiving with their loved ones, including a rare appearance from Billy Ray’s son Christopher Cody Cyrus, whom the singer welcomed with ex-girlfriend Kristin Luckey.

“Happy Thanksgiving!” Billy Ray captioned his Nov. 26 Instagram carousel. “I am so thankful for this moment - grateful for this time with my incredible son Cody, his amazing wife Nicole and my beautiful grandson Hudson. Feeling truly blessed.”

As for Cody, while he leads a far more private life then many of his Cyrus siblings—Billy Ray also adopted Tish Cyrus’ kids Brandi Cyrus, 39, and Trace Cyrus, 37, during their marriage, in addition to the pair welcoming Miley Cyrus, 34, Braison Cyrus, 32, and Noah Cyrus, 26—he did attend Miley’s nuptials to Maxx Morando on Nov. 21.

For a closer look at how Cody fits into the larger Cyrus family tree, read on.

Billy Ray Cyrus married Tish Cyrus (née Leticia Finley) on Dec. 28, 2003.

When the "Achy Breaky Heart" singer married Tish, he adopted her daughter Brandi Cyrus (born May 26, 1987) and son Trace Cyrus (Feb. 24, 1989), whose biological father is their mom's ex-husband Baxter Helson.

Tish and Billy Ray's youngest, daughter Noah Cyrus, was born Jan. 8, 2000.

From 2006 to 2010, Billy Ray played the father of Miley's normal-kid-who-moonlights-as-a-pop-star character in the Disney Channel sitcom Hannah Montana and a 2009 film adaptation.

Billy Ray and Tish announced in October 2010 that they were getting divorced, but by the following year were back together.

And at the same time, Firerose, who had been such a light of positivity, such a best friend. As for her dad's next chapter, however, a source close to Miley told E! News in October 2022 that she wasn't in love with it and didn't have a relationship with her future stepmom.

Billy Ray told People that November, however, that his family had "no hard feelings" about his engagement.

"Everybody's turning the page," he said. "It's been a lot, but everyone knew that it was time for a change."

He and Firerose got married on Oct. 10, 2023, calling it the "beautiful, joyous day that our two souls united as one in holy matrimony."

Only Some of Miley's Family Get Their Flowers

Whatever rift opened up between Miley and her dad apparently hadn't been repaired by the night of the 2024 Grammys on Feb. 4.

Tish and Brandi were there, as was Miley's boyfriend Maxx Morando, and they all got shout-outs when the "Flowers" singer won Record of the Year.

As Miley concluded her speech, "I don't think I forgot anyone."

"I'm so sorry but will you pleeeeeass just choke on the fattest c--k," Noah wrote in response. "Just for a lil bit. Great thanks."

However, Billy Ray amended his plan and filed for divorce, which was settled that August.

#719. EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit

The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.

European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.

This might be the first step to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.

During the delegations' meeting, Burnham said the deal was a "landmark agreement," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it a "turning point" in relations.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"This is a good day for Britain. This is a good day for Europe," Burnham said.

Speaking at the joint press conference, European Council President Antonio Costa said the bloc respected the British decision to leave the EU and would respect its choice to strengthen ties in the post-Brexit era.

He said jokingly that the EU and UK "may drive on the opposite sides of the road, but what matters is they are heading for the same direction."

Burnham said that the deals were made with young people in mind, adding: "This deal is for you. This deal really is about lifting your life chances."

He went further and said "Brexit took opportunities from young people," and that they have to "open up new opportunities" for young people.

Von der Leyen said the youth experience project would "open horizons and create friendships that will last a lifetime."

She said the trade agreement is a "two way street" and it means "more choice for the customers."

Von der Leyen also mentioned the agreement on the carbon market, saying that it would cut emissions and generate investments in cleaner industries.

She also said Britain will rejoin the Erasmus+ program, adding, "We miss them so much."

Burnham said the agreements reached Friday, however, represent the most the UK could achieve at the moment, "What we are announcing today is probably ‌the limit of what we can achieve in this ‌Parliament, given what needs ‌to be done to implement it."

In September, Burnham said he would seek a political consensus on the country's future relationship with the EU, even suggesting he could campaign to take Britain back into the bloc at the next election.

"Britain and Europe share values, interests and a global neighborhood. In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together. A closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe," Burnham said as he arrived in Brussels.

The three key agreements establish ways to:

The "youth experience scheme" would allow 100,000 people under 30 from each side to reside for up to three years in each other's territory for work, study or travel without being subject to existing visa requirements.

No deal was reached on tuition fees for EU students studying in Britain, a deal-breaker for the bloc. The EU has pressed for the UK to reduce university tuition fees for EU students to the same level paid by British students

"There will be further discussions coming out of it on issues including on tuition fees," Burnham said.

Von der Leyen ‌said ⁠she was confident negotiators would reach a ​solution ​on ‌tuition fees, "We will be working ‌on that in ‌the ​next month and as we have a ​track record of finding ⁠solutions,."

On the food deal, the EU and UK have agreed to scrap certificates and border checks on food and animal products to ease post-Brexit trade. In return, Britain will align more closely with EU food safety and animal health rules.

They also agreed to link their emissions-trading systems, allowing them to recognize each other's carbon allowances and exempt traded goods from carbon border taxes.

According to the AFP news agency, London estimates the deal could boost the British economy by 3.8 billion pounds annually, and spare 6.5 billion pounds worth of steel, aluminum and other industrial exports from additional taxation.

Leaders said they will establish a "structured dialogue on migration." Their joint summit statement said this would include "engagement with third countries" and "returns to third countries," among other issues.

The two sides agreed to launch formal talks on economic security and strengthen cooperation on export controls and supply chains, among other areas.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

On Monday, Burnham said it ​was the "obvious truth" that ‌Britain had lost more than it had gained from Brexit.

Polling firm YouGov runs a regular tracker on whether the UK was right or wrong to vote to quit.

Since mid-2022, a majority of people surveyed said Britain was wrong to leave.In September, the "Bregret" camp rose to 60% — the highest ever.

#717. Gibbs-White stars, Fofana struggles - player ratings for Forest v Chelsea

Premier League highlights: Nottingham Forest 3-2 Chelsea

Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice as Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea at the City Ground for the first time since 1997.

Igor Jesus' brilliant volley opened the scoring after just five minutes, before Gibbs-White struck twice in the second half as Chelsea were consigned to a fourth defeat in five matches.

Forest ran out 3-2 winners despite Emmanuel Emegha twice pulling goals back.

Here's how I rated the players and how you rated the players.

Matz Sels: The Belgian goalkeeper could do little about Emegha's goals but did not need to make many saves. 6

Jair Cunha: Cunha made one brilliant last-ditch tackle in the second half as Chelsea pushed for an equaliser. 7

Nikola Milenkovic: The Serbian was solid in the middle of the back three but otherwise unremarkable. 7

Murillo: The Brazilian centre-back made a host of important tackles and no-nonsense clearances throughout. He set the tone for a physical display and had a powerful volley saved. 7

Daniel Munoz: A typically energetic presence on the right, he also set up the opening goal. 7

James McAtee: The midfielder was good in possession but his shots lacked threat. His set-piece delivery was also poor. He did, however, win a few fouls for his team to take the pressure off. 7

Xaver Schlager: The combative midfielder set the tone early by winning the ball back in Chelsea's half on multiple occasions. He screened the backline well as Chelsea pushed for an equaliser. His wonderful pass through the eye of the needle created Forest's third. 9

Neco Williams: The Welshman battled hard with Pedro Neto in a tactical contest that ended with both players emerging with credit. 7

Igor Jesus: His sensational first-time volley opened the scoring just five minutes into the match, while the rest of his play was neat and tidy. 8

Morgan Gibbs-White: The forward scored his first goal in 11 games against Chelsea from the penalty spot in the second half. He took that chance and then another when played through by Schlager. 8

Liam Delap: The former Chelsea striker proved his worth to Forest by leading the line brilliantly, carrying a threat, looking dangerous in transition and ultimately winning a penalty for his side. 8

Subs not used: John Victor, Netz, Diomande, Yates, Hudson-Odoi, Kalimuendo

Chelsea have now lost four of their past five games

Emiliano Martinez: The Argentine goalkeeper was sent the wrong way from the spot and could not have saved Jesus' volley but made a couple of other saves. 6

Josh Acheampong: The young defender played within himself at the City Ground. 5

Wesley Fofana: The Frenchman was booed by his own supporters and told he is "not welcome here". It was a tough end to a horrible week which only got worse as he gave away the penalty having first been caught under a long ball. He was substituted in the 56th minute while also on a yellow card. 3

Moises Caicedo: A shock selection to start at centre-back for first time in his 210 games in English football, the Ecuadorian looked out of sorts with possession and in his positioning. He failed to cover for Fofana before he gave away the penalty. 5

Pep Chavarria: The Spanish full-back was an anonymous presence but did not make any obvious mistakes. 5

Romeo Lavia: The Belgian recovered from a poor touch early on to set the tempo for possession domination and his passes had real purpose. 7

Jordan Henderson: The 36-year-old was one of the weaker Chelsea performers as he filled in for now-defender Caicedo. 5

Pedro Neto: The Portuguese winger showed impressive work-rate competing with Williams, while threatened with his running in behind. His second-half shot was blocked but led to Chelsea's first goal, while his cross set up his side's second. 7

Cole Palmer: The forward was creative and highly involved for Chelsea but could not deliver that moment. It owed more to his team-mates not performing than himself. 6

Morgan Rogers: Rogers squandered multiple chances, including a huge opportunity to equalise from a corner midway through the second half. 4

Danny Welbeck: The 35-year-old striker had absolutely no service but was also completely anonymous in the first half and was taken off at the interval. 4

Emmanuel Emegha (on 45, Welbeck): An outstanding second-half display, with a brilliant touch and shot to pull one after the ball deflected into his path. He headed in a second at the far post. It raises the question about why he did not start having also scored against Leeds last weekend. 8

Levi Colwill (on 56, Fofana): The England international will be frustrated to have been dropped for a midfielder but was forced on amid Fofana's struggles and did not have much chance to shine. 5

Subs not used: Penders, Gusto, Barco, Nicoll-Jazuli, Estevao
